newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-AJAX FALTER AGAIN AS PSV KEEP 100 PERCENT RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX FALTER AGAIN AS PSV KEEP 100 PERCENT RECORD.

text.p: Dutch league champions Ajax Amsterdam continued their faltering start to the season when they lost 2-0 to lowly NEC Nijmegen while PSV Eindhoven kept their 100 percent winning record on Sunday.

Ajax, who face their first European Cup Champions' League match on Wednesday against Auxerre in France, were without key players in a poor performance that left them with two wins and just two goals from their first five games.

NEC, whose victory was their first of the campaign and lifted them from 17th to 12th, took the lead in the 18th minute when Maurice Greaf, the smallest man on the field, headed the ball behind goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar.
Ajax failed to make the most of their few chances, and Anton Janssen scored in the closing seconds of the match to seal NEC`s success.
"Ajax have a problem with their scoring ability. When you don't score on a few chances the other side will make a goal," coach Louis van Gaal said afterwards.
PSV's Rene Eykelkamp and Wim Jonk both scored twice and Belgian midfielder Marc Degryse got one goal as the Eindhoven team swept to a 5-0 home win over NAC Breda.
PSV coach Dick Advocaat, whose side have won five out of five in the league, said it was too early to celebrate the eight-point gap between his leaders and Ajax.
"But now we can afford to drop a point somewhere, something which was impossible last year. That is more relaxing," said the former Dutch national coach.
PSV lead with 15 points from five matches, followed by Feyenoord Rotterdam with 13.
Feyenoord remained unbeaten on Saturday when the were too strong for Willem II Tilburg with a 4-1 victory.
